title: Finite-stalk filtered approximation through generic direct image and cohomology
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated integral scheme, $K=k(X)$, $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ its generic point, and $M$ a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}K$. There exist a small filtered category $I$, a diagram $F:I\to\operatorname{Ab}((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}})$ and compatible maps $\iota_i:F_i\to M$ such that every $F_i$ is torsion with finite stalk at $\operatorname{Spec}\overline K$, these maps exhibit $M$ as their colimit, and for every $q\geq0$ the maps $H^q(X,\eta_*F_i)\to H^q(X,\eta_*M)$ exhibit the latter group as their colimit. The index category may have the universe of the geometric stalk; no cardinality bound on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 4: directed union of finite stable submodules and passage to cohomology

proof.text: Use [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] to identify $M$ with a torsion discrete continuous Galois module $A$. Each orbit is finite: its stabilizer is open and has finite index in the compact Galois group. Finitely many orbits generate a finite stable subgroup, since $A$ is torsion and the group generated by finitely many torsion elements is finite. The finite stable subgroups cover $A$ and their sums are again finite stable subgroups, so they form a filtered poset. This works also for $A=0$, where the zero subgroup is an index.

Transport this union cocone through the equivalence. Equivalences preserve colimits and identify the underlying stalks, so it is a colimit cocone of torsion finite-stalk sheaves with point $M$. The indexing type has the universe of $A$, not necessarily that of the underlying scheme.

The generic-point morphism is affine: the preimage of an affine open is empty or $\operatorname{Spec}K$. On a qcqs etale basis its generic fibres are finite unions of finite separable field spectra. Generic direct image evaluates to finite products of invariants, and invariants commute with the union of stable subgroups, since being fixed is tested on the same element in the subgroup and in the union. Thus generic direct image preserves this cocone. The descriptions of generic-fibre sections follow by Yoneda and [lem-exc-etale-sheaves-gsets-point], which identifies the stalk of the representable sheaf of a finite separable field extension with its Galois set of embeddings.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-directed-cohomology-colimit] to the nonempty directed poset of finite stable subgroups. This existing declaration allows the index universe u+1, matching the geometric stalk. Transport its derived-cohomology image cocone through the natural Ext/derived-global-sections comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison]. Naturality identifies every leg with the Sheaf.functorH image of the corresponding coprojection.

    (M : Sheaf (Spec X.functionField).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hM : M.IsTorsion) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (Spec X.functionField).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (ι : F ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj M),
      (∀ i, (F.obj i).IsTorsion) ∧
      (∀ i, Finite (((pointSmallEtale
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap X.functionField (AlgebraicClosure X.functionField))))).sheafFiber
            (A := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj (F.obj i))) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk M ι)) ∧
      ∀ q : ℕ, Nonempty (IsColimit
        (((Etale.lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} X.fromSpecFunctionField) ⋙
          Sheaf.functorH X.smallEtaleTopology q).mapCocone (Cocone.mk M ι)))
